Josh — thanks again for your time on the call today. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Summary: You are evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a high-compliance, patient-data use case across several clinics. Main asks were: confirmation on what prompt/output PII is stored, retention windows, audit/logging controls, and whether data can be restricted to US residency.
- What we shared on the call: hosted vs dedicated differences (Dedicated: customer-only pools, option for private control plane), and our default logging/retention posture.
- Action items for Redwood: 1) Provide a concise written confirmation on prompts/outputs — what is stored, where (region), and retention windows; 2) Provide a short diagram of data flow for Dedicated + Private (attached); 3) Share our SOC2/infosec QA items if needed.

I’ve attached the dataflow diagram and a short QA summary for quick review. I’ve copied Aditya (serving/runtime) for any kernel/implementation details and Marissa for privacy/compliance language.

Next step: Can you confirm whether Acme prefers: (A) logs/telemetry retained by Redwood for X days, with export enabled, or (B) zero retention on hosted and using the Private control plane? We’ll prepare a formal note once you confirm the preferred residency/retention approach.

Neha — appreciate the detailed recap and attachments. A few clarifying questions from our privacy team before we move to procurement: 

1) When you say "prompts & outputs" are stored "for telemetry/quality monitoring" — can you confirm exactly what is persisted for hosted vs Dedicated vs Private? Specifically: are full prompt+output pairs ever stored by Redwood in hosted/Dedicated?
2) Retention: what are the default windows (tokens/records) and can they be customized per-account?
3) Residency: we need all data (prompts, outputs, logs, and any cached KV) to remain within US regions only. Is that supported for Redwood Dedicated?
4) Access: who at Redwood can access stored prompt/output data (SRE, Support, Product) and is access logged and auditable?

We’re balancing time-to-production with compliance — if you can give declarative answers we can share them with our privacy/legal team.

Josh — thanks, great questions. Below is a concise confirmation and the current Redwood posture for prompts/outputs and related telemetry. I’m keeping Aditya and Marissa in the loop for any technical or legal clarifications.

1) What is stored (prompts & outputs):
- Hosted API (default): for customers on Redwood Hosted, prompt+output pairs are persisted for a configurable retention window used for telemetry, model quality monitoring, and abuse detection. By default we retain 90 days of prompt/output pairs. 
- Redwood Dedicated (customer-dedicated pools): by default, prompt/output content can be persisted for 30 days for debugging/ops and performance tuning; we offer an option to reduce that to 0 days (no persistence) when customers enable the "no-persist" policy on Dedicated or run through our Private control plane.
- Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem): customer controls data persistence — Redwood-managed control plane can be configured to never persist prompt/output pairs; if using customer-managed on-prem components, persistence is entirely under customer control.

2) Retention customization:
- Retention windows are configurable at the account or deployment level (30/90/365/0 days). Longer retention requires a reviewed policy and is subject to contract.

3) Residency:
- Dedicated: we support region-pin for Dedicated pools (US-only). All persistent storage and logs for a region-pinned Dedicated deployment are kept in the selected cloud region(s) in the US.
- Hosted: default is multi-region; we can discuss region restrictions for enterprise customers via Dedicated or Private.

4) Access & auditing: 
- Access: Support/SRE/Platform engineers require explicit, time-bound access approvals for viewing prompt/output content. We enforce a least-privilege model.
- Auditing: all access to stored prompt/output content is logged and available for audit; logs include user, timestamp, justification, and TTL of access. We can provide filtered audit logs for the account for SOC2/attestation purposes.

5) Caching/kv: transient KV cache used for inference is in-memory on serving nodes; for Dedicated/Private there is no cross-customer KV sharing. Persistent caches are only used when explicitly enabled and follow same residency/retention as above.

6) Recommendation for Acme given your constraints: we recommend Dedicated with US-region pin + no-persist flag enabled for prompt/output persistence, and export of audit logs to your SIEM. That gives the shortest path to production while meeting residency & retention requirements.

I’ve asked Aditya to add a short note on how we implement the no-persist flag and the telemetry tiering (keeps only token-level metrics vs full text) — linking below.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Josh — following up with the implementation note Neha promised. Short, technical confirmation below: 

- "no-persist" flag: when enabled on Dedicated or Private, the inference path disables write-through to persistent stores for prompt+output pairs. Requests are still served from the runtime; transient traces (in-memory) exist for in-flight debugging for up to the configured TTL but are never written to S3/long-term storage.
- Telemetry tiers: we support three telemetry tiers: minimal (token counts, latency histograms), standard (aggregated metrics + sampling of token-level metrics), and full (sampled prompt/output pairs). For Dedicated with no-persist + minimal telemetry, we only store aggregated metrics and no text.
- Access controls: debug dumps that are required for incident postmortems require a manager-approved access ticket; those tickets are logged and exported to the customer audit log on request.

If useful, I can put together a one-page technical appendix for your security team that they can attach to the SOW.

—Aditya
